pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` in the environment. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking
- [Merge own PRs](merge-own-prs.md) — squash-merge my green PRs in surveybeat-next without asking

# Comment themes are computed once at close, need two comments, never quote, and can't be edited

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the Organization Durable Object asks the model for at most 5 Comment themes over the Round's redacted comments (ADR 0009). Each theme is a short label and one neutral sentence. The model also returns which comments support each theme, and the object keeps only themes supported by **at least two comments**. The result is stored with the Round's Result and never recomputed.

**Who sees what.** Members see each theme's label and sentence, never raw comments and never counts. The Lead sees the themes, how many comments support each, and the redacted raw comments, as in Release 1. Comments that fit no theme with two supporters stay visible only to the Lead.

**No quotes.** The prompt and the JSON schema ask for paraphrase, and a check rejects any theme that repeats 6 or more consecutive words of a comment; a rejected theme is dropped, not repaired. Exact wording or a personal style can identify the author.

**Failure.** The call retries with backoff for up to 24 hours. Until it succeeds, Results show "Themes are being prepared"; after that, Results stand without themes. The Review window (#89) never waits for themes.

**No editing.** The Lead cannot edit, hide, or reorder themes. A Lead who could hide an unflattering theme before sharing would undercut trust before features (SPEC §3.1).

## Considered options

- **Themes from a single comment:** rejected. Shown to the whole Team, a one-comment theme is one person's words in other words.
- **Redacted quotes under each theme** (the old glossary wording): rejected for the same reason as quotes in the sentence.
- **Recomputing themes on view:** rejected. It would call the model on every view, could change what people already saw, and needs the comments sent again.

## Consequences

- The privacy rule table gains rows: a theme never shown below N, never with fewer than two supporting comments, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, and never shown to members with counts.
- Small Teams with few comments often get no themes; the Lead still has the raw comments.
- Themes exist only for Rounds that close after AI processing is turned on.
# The discussion guide is written by the AI, in the same call as the themes, for the Lead only

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the call that writes the Comment themes (ADR 0016) also writes the Round's discussion guide. It has four sections: what stood out, what people raised, Actions to check on, and at most 3 questions to ask the Team. A Round without comments still gets a guide from its scores and Actions.

**Input.** This extends ADR 0015's list of what may be sent: the Dimension scores and changes (with which are flagged as larger than usual), the redacted comments, the Question text, and the titles of open Actions passed through the same Redaction (ADR 0009). Never an Action owner, a Person, or any name, id, or time.

**Rules.** The guide never quotes (the 6-word-run check of ADR 0016 applies to every section), never says or guesses who said what, and must match a strict JSON schema. A guide that fails a check is dropped as a whole.

**No AI, no guide.** There is no rule-based fallback. With AI processing off, the Lead sees a line saying an Organization admin can turn it on. If the call fails for 24 hours, the Round has no guide.

**Lead only, as generated.** The guide is stored with the Result, generated once, shown only to the Lead on the Results page with a "Copy as text" button, and cannot be edited in SurveyBeat. After the conversation, the Lead can write a Note on the Results page that the Team sees.

## Considered options

- **Rules-written guide with optional AI questions:** rejected by the product owner; the guide is the AI's job.
- **A separate call for the guide:** rejected; it would send the comments twice.

## Consequences

- The guide exists only for Organizations that turn AI processing on, and only for Rounds that close afterwards.
- The privacy rule table gains rows for the guide: never below N, never shown to members, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, never naming an Action owner.

# Comment themes are computed once at close, need two comments, never quote, and can't be edited

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the Organization Durable Object asks the model for at most 5 Comment themes over the Round's redacted comments (ADR 0009). Each theme is a short label and one neutral sentence. The model also returns which comments support each theme, and the object keeps only themes supported by **at least two comments**. The result is stored with the Round's Result and never recomputed.

**Who sees what.** Members see each theme's label and sentence, never raw comments and never counts. The Lead sees the themes, how many comments support each, and the redacted raw comments, as in Release 1. Comments that fit no theme with two supporters stay visible only to the Lead.

**No quotes.** The prompt and the JSON schema ask for paraphrase, and a check rejects any theme that repeats 6 or more consecutive words of a comment; a rejected theme is dropped, not repaired. Exact wording or a personal style can identify the author.

**Failure.** The call retries with backoff for up to 24 hours. Until it succeeds, Results show "Themes are being prepared"; after that, Results stand without themes. The Review window (#89) never waits for themes.

**No editing.** The Lead cannot edit, hide, or reorder themes. A Lead who could hide an unflattering theme before sharing would undercut trust before features (SPEC §3.1).

## Considered options

- **Themes from a single comment:** rejected. Shown to the whole Team, a one-comment theme is one person's words in other words.
- **Redacted quotes under each theme** (the old glossary wording): rejected for the same reason as quotes in the sentence.
- **Recomputing themes on view:** rejected. It would call the model on every view, could change what people already saw, and needs the comments sent again.

## Consequences

- The privacy rule table gains rows: a theme never shown below N, never with fewer than two supporting comments, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, and never shown to members with counts.
- Small Teams with few comments often get no themes; the Lead still has the raw comments.
- Themes exist only for Rounds that close after AI processing is turned on.
# The discussion guide is written by the AI, in the same call as the themes, for the Lead only

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the call that writes the Comment themes (ADR 0016) also writes the Round's discussion guide. It has four sections: what stood out, what people raised, Actions to check on, and at most 3 questions to ask the Team. A Round without comments still gets a guide from its scores and Actions.

**Input.** This extends ADR 0015's list of what may be sent: the Dimension scores and changes (with which are flagged as larger than usual), the redacted comments, the Question text, and the titles of open Actions passed through the same Redaction (ADR 0009). Never an Action owner, a Person, or any name, id, or time.

**Rules.** The guide never quotes (the 6-word-run check of ADR 0016 applies to every section), never says or guesses who said what, and must match a strict JSON schema. A guide that fails a check is dropped as a whole.

**No AI, no guide.** There is no rule-based fallback. With AI processing off, the Lead sees a line saying an Organization admin can turn it on. If the call fails for 24 hours, the Round has no guide.

**Lead only, as generated.** The guide is stored with the Result, generated once, shown only to the Lead on the Results page with a "Copy as text" button, and cannot be edited in SurveyBeat. After the conversation, the Lead can write a Note on the Results page that the Team sees.

## Considered options

- **Rules-written guide with optional AI questions:** rejected by the product owner; the guide is the AI's job.
- **A separate call for the guide:** rejected; it would send the comments twice.

## Consequences

- The guide exists only for Organizations that turn AI processing on, and only for Rounds that close afterwards.
- The privacy rule table gains rows for the guide: never below N, never shown to members, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, never naming an Action owner.
